newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Portugese, Irish fastest carbon dioxide dumpers-UN.
newsitem.headline: Portugese, Irish fastest carbon dioxide dumpers-UN.

text.p: Portugal, Ireland and Denmark dumped energy-related carbon dioxide into the atmosphere faster than any other industrialised countries in the five years to 1995, a United Nations economic report said on Wednesday.

The annual U.N. world economic and social survey issued in Geneva said the United States remained the biggest source of carbon dioxide emissions which are in part to blame for warming the earth's atmosphere.
Washington faces criticism for refusing to back a European Union target of a 15 percent reduction in gas emissions from 1990 levels by 2010.
U.S. energy-related carbon dioxide emissions rose nearly six percent in the five years over 1990, the U.N. report said.

In the same period, Britain, Austria, France, Germany, Italy and Switzerland were the only industrialised nations that cut carbon dioxide emissions, which are mainly caused by burning fossil fuels such as oil, natural gas and coal, over 1990 levels.
The biggest cuts over 1990 were 7.6 percent in Germany, 5.5 percent in Switzerland and five percent in Britain.
But the U.N. report said such cuts were offset by higher emissions elsewhere.
The highest growth rates in energy-related carbon dioxide emissions in 1990-1995 were in Portugal with 48.1 percent, Denmark with 24.5 percent and Ireland with 21.9 percent.
This compared to an average 4.6 percent growth in energy-related carbon dioxide emissions in the same period among member states of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Emissions also grew in Turkey by 16.3 percent, Sweden by 16 percent, Iceland by 12.1 percent, the Netherlands by 10.4 percent and Greece by 10.2 percent in the same period.
